stem: A government officer's real salary was Rs 25,000 per month in terms of base year 2016 prices. The price index for 2024 with 2016 as base year (= 100) is 160. What nominal salary should the officer receive in 2024 to maintain the same real purchasing power?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Nominal salary = Real salary x Price index / 100 = 25000 x 160 / 100 = Rs 40,000. This is the reverse of deflation: multiplying by the index restores the nominal figure.
Dividing the real salary by the index instead of multiplying: 25000 / 160 x 100 = 15625. This deflates an already-real figure, producing a doubly deflated (and nonsensical) answer.
Adding the index value to the real salary: 25000 + 160 = 25160. This treats the index as an additive adjustment rather than a multiplicative ratio.
Computing 25000 x 160 / 100 but misplacing the decimal: arriving at 400 instead of 40000 by dividing by 10000 rather than 100.

explanation: When the real value is known and you need the nominal value, reverse the deflation formula: Nominal = Real x (Index / 100). Here: 25000 x 160 / 100 = Rs 40,000. The 60-point rise in the index means prices are 60% higher, so nominal pay must rise by 60% to preserve purchasing power.

explanation_sections.punchline: To find the nominal figure from a real figure, multiply by the index ratio - the exact reverse of deflation.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the reverse-deflation formula: Nominal = Real x Index / 100. Map: Real = 25000, Index = 160. Compute: 25000 x 1.6 = 40000.
explanation_sections.lesson: Deflation divides by (index/100); reverse deflation multiplies. Never apply the same direction twice.
explanation_sections.timing: About 45 seconds. Trap: option 2 (Rs 15,625) is the result of deflating again - confirm you are going in the right direction before computing.
